content: The polynomial is \(2x^4 + a_3 x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_1 x + 1 = 0\) with integer coefficients. By the Rational Root Theorem, any rational root \(\frac{p}{q}\) in lowest terms must have \(p\) dividing the constant term (1) and \(q\) dividing the leading coefficient (2). Thus \(p \in \{\pm 1\}\) and \(q \in \{1, 2\}\). The distinct possible rational roots are \(\pm 1\) and \(\pm \frac{1}{2}\), giving 4 different values. All four are achievable for some choice of integers \(a_3, a_2, a_1\). A
